newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias drops 8.70 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Victorias drops 8.70 pct in late trade.

text.p: The Philippines' biggest sugar miller Victorias Milling Co fell 40 centavos, or 8.70 percent, to 4.20 pesos in late trade Monday on news that its creditors are yet to receive interest payments on its 4.423 billion peso debts, brokers said.
"It's because of talk that creditors are still waiting for interest payments from Victorias," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.

Two of Victorias 32 creditors said on Monday that the interest money amounting to 110 million pesos was deposited by Victorias with one or two banks that were meant to disburse it to the other creditors.
But the distribution of the interest payments were delayed due to operational reasons, they said.
"There was recovery on Victorias and so some investors are taking profits. It's also related to the interest payment issue," said Jonas Ferrer, vice-president at Pryce Securities.
Victorias officials were not immediately available to comment on the status of its debt interest payments.
Last Friday, a Victorias official said the company had enough funds to make interest payments due that day.
A total of 171,000 Victorias shares valued at 747,000 pesos were traded late in Tuesday's session.
